current_bottleneck: Bounded postforecast widening is capped. State-score and per-cell/horizon interval-scale adapters both improve aggregate coverage but fail lower-only regime/cell inclusion and damage scenario authenticity. The hard blocker is not generic width but sparse stress-path allocation in specific cells/regimes/windows.
last_result_summary: 603a tested a bounded per-cell/per-horizon widening table around frozen 510a: target coverage 0.95, high-side cap disabled, no regime bins, candidate scale range [1.0, 2.0], fitted range 1.075/1.475/1.900. It scored 4/11, with coverage 84.5% and h1/h7/h14/h30 coverage 89.7/82.5/84.7/82.4, but regime layer2 stayed 0/8, persistent severe undercoverage stayed 7.3%, daily-change KS was 13/25, level KS 1/25, and per-cell extreme-jump scale 14/25. Risk-readiness still failed; worst lower-only cell improved only to 0.556 and worst regime cell only to 0.360.
next_step_recommendation: Do not run another scale-table/postforecast widening variant. The next principled step is post-experiment analysis or paradigm ideation focused on sparse stress allocation: either identify a mechanism that can change path direction/location while preserving authenticity, or document that available conditioning data are insufficient and specify the needed additional state variables.
